standard.title: Glossary of Terms Relating to Iron and Steel (Part 1 to Part 8)
standard.description: This standard is a multi-part master national glossary that establishes standardized definitions, processing terms, classification rules, and testing/metallurgical terminology for iron, steel, and associated heavy manufacturing operations in India. By unifying terms across raw material extraction, steelmaking, rolling, forging, heat-treating, and mechanical testing, this standard eliminates ambiguity in commercial contracts, product standards, customs classifications, and quality control audits.

revision_history: First Edition (published as a single comprehensive glossary under the designation IS 1956 : 1962), 1962
First Reorganization into Parts (split into separate parts to accommodate the rapid technological expansion of specialized steel manufacturing, testing, and processing industries), 1975-1976

Second Revisions (Part 2 revised in 2018, Part 3 in 2019, Part 4 in 2013 to align with modern international EN, ISO, and ASTM terminologies and accommodate newly formulated micro-alloyed and advanced high-strength steel grades), 2013-2019

amendments.summary: No active amendments have been issued on the latest active revisions of these parts.

certification.description: Master National Reference Glossary. IS 1956 is not a product specification and therefore does not carry a separate mandatory or voluntary BIS license or ISI certification mark. However, its terminology, material definitions, chemical alloying boundaries (such as the definition of stainless steel as containing >= 12% chromium), and defect classifications are legally binding and universally referenced in national sales tax/customs litigation, heavy engineering disputes, procurement contracts, and trade arbitrations to resolve definition ambiguities. Precious metal hallmarking is completely inapplicable.
requirements: Establishes definitions for core metallurgical phenomena, heat treatment processes (such as Annealing, Normalizing, Quenching, and Tempering), and mechanical testing methodologies (tension, hardness, impact). This part is frequently used in tax and customs disputes to define raw material boundaries (e.g. defining 'Alloy' vs. 'Alloy Steel' or defining 'Stainless Steel' as an alloy steel containing 12% or more chromium).

Covers terms relating to the raw chemistry and liquid-state processing of steel. Defines terms for furnace technologies (such as Basic Oxygen Furnace/LD converter, Electric Arc Furnace, and Induction Furnace), refining, casting (ingot and continuous casting), and deoxidation practices (rimmed, capped, semi-killed, and killed steels).

Defines physical wrought shapes characterized by linear axes. Standardizes terms for structural sections (beams, channels, angles), merchant bars, wire rods, hot-rolled wires, and reinforcing steel bars.

Defines hot-rolled and cold-rolled flat-wound products. Establishes definitions for sheets, strips, plates, and wide coils, along with sheet metal defects (such as surface lamination, scaling, edge cracking, and stretcher strain lines).
Covers cold-finished long products. Defines terms for bright steel bars (produced by cold drawing, turning, or grinding), wire drawing processes, and wire properties.

Defines hot and cold plastic deformation processes using dies. Standardizes terms distinguishing open die forging (free forging), closed die forging (impression die forging), flash, trim, die cavities, and forging defects.
Regulates traditional slag-bearing fibrous wrought iron products. Defines terms for puddling, muck bars, and refined wrought iron shapes.

Defines hollow structural and fluid-conveying sections. Standardizes terms distinguishing seamless tubes (produced by hot piercing and cold drawing) and welded pipes (electric resistance welded, spiral welded), along with tube fittings and sizing terms.
